---
title: "Sugar Pines Sampled in Yosemite and Sequoia National Park"
format: html
---

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

library(leaflet)

# 1. Read the CSV file into R
my_data <- read.csv("2026data.csv")

# 2. define icons
tree_icons <- awesomeIcons(
  icon = "tree", # tree icon
  library = "fa", # Tells Leaflet to pull from Font Awesome
    # Pin background: red for "i", light green for "r"
  markerColor = ifelse(my_data$resistance == "I", "lightred", "green"),
  # Tree symbol: dark red for "i", dark green for "r"
  iconColor = ifelse(my_data$resistance == "I", "#660000", "#1B4332")
)

# 3. Pass the data frame to leaflet()
leaflet(data = my_data) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addAwesomeMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude,
    icon = tree_icons,
    popup = ~paste0(
      "<b>Site ID:</b> ", plotID, "<br>",
      "<b>Tree ID:</b> ", treeID, "<br>",
      "<b>Resistance:</b> ", resistance, "<br>",
      "<b>Date collected:</b> ", date
    )
  )
```
  
# Red Trees indicate Sugar Pines infected with white pine blister rust (WPBR)
# Green Trees represent Sugar Pines resistant to WPBR
